questions.question: A thief saw a policeman, and he started running at a speed of 18 m/s. After 12 seconds, the policeman starts running behind the thief at a certain speed. If the policeman covered 864 meters distance to reach the thief, then the speed (in m/s) of the policeman is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of thief (Sₜₕᵢₑf) = 18 m/s

Time taken by thief to start running before policeman starts = 12 seconds

Distance covered by policeman to catch the thief (Dₚₒₗᵢ꜀ₑₘₐₙ) = 864 meters

**Calculations:**

Distance covered by the thief in 12 seconds:

⇒ Dₜₕᵢₑf = Sₜₕᵢₑf × Time = 18 × 12 = 216 meters

Total distance between thief and policeman when policeman starts running = 216 m

Distance covered by thief while policeman was chasing = 864 - 216 = 648 m

The time taken by the thief to cover this distance = 648/18 = 36 seconds.

Which means the time taken by the policeman to reach the thief = 36 seconds

Speed of policeman = Total Distance /Total time

⇒ 864 / 36 = 24m/s

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The ratio of the present age of A and B is 3 : 1. Five years ago, the ratio of their ages was 5 : 1. The age of A (in years) after eight years will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The present age ratio of A and B = 3 : 1

Five years ago, their age ratio = 5 : 1

Calculation:

Let the present ages of A and B be 3x and x respectively.

Five years ago, their ages were (3x - 5) and (x - 5).

(3x - 5)/(x - 5) = (5)/(1)

⇒ 3x - 5 = 5(x - 5)

⇒ 3x - 5 = 5x - 25

⇒ 3x - 5x = -25 + 5

⇒ -2x = -20

⇒ x = 10

Present age of A = 3x = 3 × 10 = 30 years

Age of A after 8 years = 30 + 8 = 38 years

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A man sells an article at a certain price and suffers a loss of 20%. If he sells the article at ₹100 more, he gets a profit of 30%. Find the cost price of the article (in ₹).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man sells an article at a certain price and suffers a loss of 20%. If he sells the article at ₹100 more, he gets a profit of 30%.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 ± Profit/Loss%)

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) = x

For loss of 20%:

⇒ SP₁ = x × (1 - 20/100)

⇒ SP₁ = x × (80/100)

⇒ SP₁ = 0.8x

For profit of 30%:

⇒ SP₂ = x × (1 + 30/100)

⇒ SP₂ = x × (130/100)

⇒ SP₂ = 1.3x

Given, SP₂ = SP₁ + 100

⇒ 1.3x = 0.8x + 100

⇒ 1.3x - 0.8x = 100

⇒ 0.5x = 100

⇒ x = 100 / 0.5

⇒ x = 200

**∴ The cost price of the article is ₹200. The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Which of the following acts introduced the system of dyarchy in the provincial administration in India?

options.text: The Government of India Act of 1909
The Government of India Act of 1919
The Government of India Act of 1935
The Government of India Act of 1947

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Government of India Act of 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act of 1919** is also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**.
 
• This Act introduced the system of **dyarchy** in the provincial administration of India.
 
• **Dyarchy** refers to a dual system of governance where the provincial subjects were divided into two categories: **Reserved and Transferred subjects**.
 
• **Reserved subjects** (e.g., police, revenue, and justice) were under the control of the Governor and his Executive Council, responsible to the British government.
 
• **Transferred subjects** (e.g., agriculture, health, and education) were administered by Indian ministers who were responsible to the legislative council.
 
• The Act of 1919 aimed to gradually introduce **self-governing institutions** in India, as promised by the British government.
 
• This Act also expanded the **legislative councils** and introduced the concept of **direct elections** in India for the first time.
 
• The reforms were seen as a step towards **responsible government**, but they were criticized for limiting Indian participation and retaining significant British control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1909**__

 __
 
• Known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, this Act introduced the concept of **separate electorates** for Muslims in India.
 
• It aimed to increase Indian participation in the legislative councils by expanding their size and scope.
 
• The Act allowed for the indirect election of members to the Imperial Legislative Council.
 
• However, it did not introduce dyarchy or significant self-governance.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1935**__
 __
 
• This Act introduced **provincial autonomy** and abolished the dyarchy system in the provinces.
 
• It proposed the establishment of an **All-India Federation**, which never materialized.
 
• The Act also introduced a bicameral legislature at the Centre and extended the franchise to more people.
 
• It is considered the longest and most detailed Act passed by the British Parliament concerning India.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1947**__
 
 
• This Act, also known as the **Indian Independence Act**, marked the end of British rule in India.
 
• It partitioned British India into two independent dominions, **India and Pakistan**.
 
• The Act gave complete legislative sovereignty to the newly formed nations.
 
• It is regarded as the final legal framework for the independence of India.
